subject: One house, two Diwalis: colour and smoke
alt: Titas Panda's cartoon, in two panels. The background of the left panel is pale yellow: a boy with black curly hair, in a light green T-shirt and dark shorts, stands pouring oil from a bottle into a diya in his hand. Below him a woman in a red sari and red head-covering crouches, lighting diyas. Many diyas lie scattered on the floor, some burning with yellow flames rising. At the top left, hand-written: TITAS PANDA. The right panel's background is grey: at the bottom a young woman in a grey head-covering kneels, pouring oil from a bottle into a diya; above her an old woman in a grey head-covering stands bent, a diya in her hand, and a white puff of smoke-like breath comes from her mouth. Diyas lie on the floor, some with yellow flames, and a bottle of oil stands in front. At the top left again: TITAS PANDA.
chutki: One house, two moments. On the left, in yellow light, a boy pours oil into diyas and a mother lights them. On the right, the same diyas, the same bottle of oil, but the room is grey; now a young woman pours the oil and an old woman bends over a diya, coughing, a white puff of smoke-like breath coming from her mouth.

Titas Panda has changed not just the colour but the time. The festival's diya stays the same, but the hands that light it keep changing, and the smoke that comes with the light settles in those same old lungs. The cartoon asks who finally pays the bill for the brightness we gather.
